title: HealthStatus
description: Uniform health report for every service and provider. LIVENESS AND READINESS ARE DISTINCT and that distinction is the entire reason this contract exists: Ollama loading a 30 GB model is alive and not ready, and routing a turn to it produces a timeout that is indistinguishable from a broken assistant.

compatibility.notes: Mirrors HealthCore in contracts/grpc/v1/common.proto — KEEP THEM IN STEP. Adding a `state` value is MINOR; consumers must treat unknown states as `degraded`, which is the conservative reading. Note that this schema has five producers: that is legitimate here because health is genuinely uniform across services, and it is the one case where many producers is a feature rather than the design smell the README warns about.

live.description: Responds at all. Maps to a Kubernetes livenessProbe — false means RESTART ME.

ready.description: Can accept work right now. Maps to a readinessProbe — false means STOP SENDING TRAFFIC, but do not restart. Conflating the two causes a loading model to be killed and restarted forever.

requires_network.description: ADR-0007. True means this service CANNOT be selected at tier L0. Reported rather than assumed, so the L0 conformance gate can assert it at runtime instead of trusting configuration.

degraded_reason.description: Required when state is `degraded`. M5 requires the system to keep answering; this is what it says when asked why the answer is thinner than usual.

dependencies.description: Downstream health, one level deep only. Deeper nesting turns a health check into a distributed trace, which is what ADR-0019 is for.

examples.degraded_reason: Qdrant reachable but consolidation job is backlogged; recall quality may be reduced.
